Accountable obligation owner.value: Product Compliance owns the IIPRC eligibility determination for every life, annuity, LTC and DI product component; escalation to Regulatory Counsel on any non-Compact or mix-and-match call

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the applicable IIPRC Uniform Standard (as amended, with its adoption date), the Compact Product Filing Rule, and the enacting Compact statute of the representative member state Arizona (Title 20 of the Arizona Revised Statutes), re-read at determination time alongside D.C. Official Code Title 31 and Hawaii Revised Statutes Chapter 431

In-scope processes.value: Product change intake → Compact eligibility gate for every new or revised individual life, group term life, individual annuity, LTC and disability income form, rate schedule and rating rule intended for use in any of the 47 Compact member jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: SERFF IIPRC filing instance (Compact Filing Information tab and Filing Access) plus the Filing Determination Log held in the filing tracker

Compliance procedure documented.value: IIPRC Eligibility Determination Procedure — component decomposition, Uniform Standard mapping, member-state licensure check, opt-out and state-specific requirement check, Compact vs state vs mix-and-match path selection, and log entry before any build freeze

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel; re-approved annually and within 30 days of any IIPRC Uniform Standard amendment or membership change

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per filing — the determination must close before the product build freeze and is back-solved from the Compact's 60-day review period; a membership or opt-out change triggers re-determination within 30 days of notification

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing tracker milestone alerts at T-120/T-90/T-60 days to target effective date for every open determination, plus a standing alert on the IIPRC Filing Information Notice distribution list

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Determination worksheet, dated Uniform Standard captures, member-roster snapshot and counsel sign-off retained 7 years from withdrawal of the form or rate schedule

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any component used in a member state without a closed eligibility determination is logged as a compliance exception with root cause, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Counsel signs off every decision to file outside the Compact, every mix-and-match combination and every late determination remediation

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All life, annuity, LTC and DI product components with an effective date inside the quarter across the 47 Compact jurisdictions, taken from the policy admin form-master change log

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any component in use in a member state with no eligibility determination dated before its effective date is a fail; any incorrect Uniform Standard mapping is a fail; one or more fails escalates to the Head of Compliance

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per filing and continuous; the test runs quarterly over that quarter's component population plus 100% review of determinations that chose a non-Compact path

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have authored or approved any sampled eligibility determination

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly IIPRC eligibility test workpaper (population extract, reconciliation, sample, re-performance notes, exceptions) filed in the compliance evidence repository under REG-016-C01

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Determination log export, Uniform Standard mapping table and member-roster snapshots, presentable to an IIPRC market conduct review or a member-state examiner within 5 business days

checklist.step: Open a Compact eligibility determination for the approved product change
actions: Open the product change queue and filter Status = 'Approved for filing determination' and Line of Business in (Individual Life, Group Term Life, Individual Annuity, LTC, Disability Income).

Start a determination worksheet capturing product name, writing company and NAIC company code, target effective date, distribution states, and whether the change affects new business only or new plus in-force.
Ask the Insurance Product Dev Lead for the hard date driver (illustration release, competitor response, statutory mandate) and record it on the worksheet header.
Attach the signed change request and save the folder as IIPRC-<company>-<product>-<target effective date>.
checklist.done: the worksheet carries product, writing company, NAIC code, target date and state list with the change request attached.

checklist.step: Decompose the change into filable product components
actions: List every artifact the change touches on its own worksheet row: policy or contract form, application, rider or endorsement, amendment, schedule page, rate schedule, and rating rule.
Copy the form number and edition date exactly as printed in the form footer onto each FORM row.
Tag each row with the Compact component type used by the Commission — Policy/Contract, Application, Rider/Endorsement/Amendment, Rate Schedule, or Actuarial Memorandum support.
Mark rows that are marketing collateral, illustrations or internal procedure as NON-FILED and state why on the row.
checklist.done: every touched artifact has a row, a form number with edition date, and a Compact component type.

checklist.step: Map each component to the governing IIPRC Uniform Standard
actions: Open the Uniform Standards library on insurancecompact.org and select the product family (Individual Life, Group Term Life, Individual Deferred Non-Variable Annuity, Individual Disability Income, Individual LTC).

Identify the Core Standard and every Additional Standard the component touches (for example the Individual Deferred Non-Variable Annuity Core Standard plus the Additional Standard for Guaranteed Living Benefits).
Record the standard title, the adoption or last-amended date, and the specific section numbers the component must satisfy on each worksheet row.
Save a dated PDF capture of each standard into the determination folder named <standard>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf.
Where no Uniform Standard exists for the component, mark the row NOT COMPACT-ELIGIBLE and route it to the state-by-state filing path.
checklist.done: every component row names its Uniform Standard with adoption date and section numbers, or is marked not Compact-eligible.

checklist.step: Confirm the writing company is a registered Compact filer in good standing
actions: Check the insurer's IIPRC registration status and annual registration fee payment date with the Compact Office, and record the registration expiry.

In SERFF confirm the company instance can select the Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Commission as a filing destination and that the company profile carries the correct NAIC company code and domiciliary state.
Ask the Compliance Analyst for evidence that the writing company holds a current certificate of authority in each member state to be selected — an unlicensed state cannot be included on the filing.
Record registration expiry and the licensure evidence reference on the worksheet header.
checklist.done: registration is current, the SERFF profile resolves to the Compact, and licensure evidence exists for every state to be selected.

checklist.step: Pull the current IIPRC member roster and set the state selection
actions: Download the current member jurisdiction list from insurancecompact.org (46 states plus the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico as applicable) and save it dated into the determination folder.
Mark the non-member jurisdictions the product also needs — California, New York and any other non-member — and route those to the state-by-state filing path on a separate worksheet tab.
Confirm the representative member state Arizona (Title 20 of the Arizona Revised Statutes) is in scope for this product and record the Arizona-specific requirements reference.
Write the final Compact state selection list onto the worksheet header with the roster snapshot date.
checklist.done: a dated member-roster snapshot supports a written Compact state selection list, with non-member states split onto the state filing path.

checklist.step: Check per-state opt-outs against each mapped Uniform Standard
actions: Open the Compact's opt-out record and identify any member state that has opted out of a Uniform Standard mapped in the previous step, by legislation or by regulation.
For each opt-out hit, read the state's opt-out instrument and confirm whether the state must be dropped from the Compact selection and filed separately.
Record the opt-out state, the standard opted out of, the citation and the effective date on the affected worksheet rows.
Confirm no opt-out affects Arizona, District of Columbia (D.C. Official Code Title 31) or Hawaii (HRS Chapter 431) for the mapped standards, and note the confirmation date.
checklist.done: every mapped standard has an opt-out check with a citation, and opted-out states are removed from the Compact selection.

checklist.step: Capture the state-specific requirements that ride on a Compact filing
actions: Open the Compact's state-specific requirements chart and read the entry for every selected member state.
List the items the state still imposes on a Compact-approved product — fraud warning wording, free-look period variations, required notices, state-mandated disclosure inserts.
Hand the list to the Policy Forms Specialist so the variable bracketing in the forms can carry each state variation, and record the hand-off date.
Write the state-specific requirement count for each selected state onto the worksheet.
checklist.done: each selected member state has a written state-specific requirement list handed to Forms with a dated acknowledgement.

checklist.step: Select the filing path per component: Compact, state, or mix and match
actions: Set each worksheet row to COMPACT, STATE-BY-STATE, or MIX AND MATCH (Compact-approved component combined with a state-approved component).

For every MIX AND MATCH row, name the state-approved partner component with its state approval date and tracking number, and confirm the Compact's Mix and Match operating procedure permits the combination.
For every STATE-BY-STATE row, state the reason — no Uniform Standard, state opt-out, non-member jurisdiction, or product feature outside the standard.
Never leave a row reading only 'not Compact' without one of those named reasons.
checklist.done: every component row carries a filing path with a named justification and, for mix and match, the partner component's state approval reference.

checklist.step: Confirm which components carry a rate filing obligation
actions: Confirm with Pricing which components are LTC or disability income, where the Compact requires a rate schedule and actuarial memorandum, versus life and annuity components where rates are not separately filed with the Commission.
For LTC and DI rows, export the proposed rate schedule and the loss ratio demonstration from the actuarial model and note the model version and valuation date.
Record the rate change percentage and whether the filing is initial rates or a rate increase, since a rate increase pulls the LTC rate increase standard and its additional disclosure requirements.
Sign the rate-obligation conclusion onto the worksheet and email it to the Product Filing Specialist.
checklist.done: each component states whether a Compact rate filing is required, with the model reference and rate change percentage for LTC and DI rows.

checklist.step: Search SERFF for an existing Compact approval that already covers the component
actions: In SERFF open Filing Access, set the state to the Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Commission, and search by company name or NAIC code plus form number.
Filter Disposition to Approved and sort by disposition date descending.
Open the closest match and compare the approved form edition date and Statement of Variability against the new edition, line by line.
Decide reuse versus new filing: reuse only where the approved text is unchanged and the state selection already covers the target states.
Copy the SERFF tracking number and IIPRC approval date onto the worksheet row wherever reuse applies.
checklist.done: each row states reuse with a SERFF tracking number and approval date, or new filing, based on an inspected prior Compact filing.

checklist.step: Back-solve the latest submission date from the Compact review period
actions: Record the Compact review period for the product type (the Commission works to a 60-day review for a complete product filing) on each COMPACT row.

Add internal lead times: package preparation days, actuarial review days, and an objection-response buffer of 30 days since an unanswered objection can put the filing at risk of being deemed withdrawn.
Compute latest submission date = target effective date minus (Compact review days + objection buffer + implementation lead) and write it on the row.
Load each latest submission date into the filing calendar with T-120/T-90/T-60 reminders against the target effective date.
checklist.done: every Compact row shows the review period, the computed latest submission date and a calendar entry with reminders.

checklist.step: Write the determination rows into the Filing Determination Log
actions: Add one log row per component: change id, form number and edition, Uniform Standard and section, filing path, Compact state selection, opt-out exclusions, rate filing required Y/N, latest submission date, reuse tracking number, decider and decision date.
Link each log row to the determination folder holding the dated standard captures and the member-roster snapshot.
Set status to 'Determined — pending counsel' for STATE-BY-STATE and MIX AND MATCH rows, otherwise 'Determined — closed'.
Reject any row with a blank Uniform Standard, blank state selection or blank decision date.
checklist.done: the log holds one complete, source-linked row per component with no blank fields.

checklist.step: Obtain Regulatory Counsel sign-off on the risky calls
actions: Route to counsel every STATE-BY-STATE and every MIX AND MATCH row plus any row where a Uniform Standard was mapped by analogy rather than on point.

Re-read the cited Uniform Standard section and the member state's Compact enabling statute (for the representative state, Title 20 of the Arizona Revised Statutes) and confirm or overturn the call in writing on the row.
Send overturned rows back to the Regulatory Filing Specialist for rework within the same week and re-review before closure.
Stamp confirmed rows with counsel name and date and move them to 'Determined — closed'.
checklist.done: no non-Compact or mix-and-match row is closed without a dated counsel confirmation on the log row.

checklist.step: Arm the pre-use gate on the product change record
actions: Attach the determination summary to the product change record and publish it to the release plan.
Set the pre-use gate flag on every Compact component: no form may be issued and no rate used in any member state until the Commission's approval is recorded against the component.
Give the implementation team the per-state earliest-use dates so form availability in policy admin is dated from the approval, not from the build date.
Add the Compact submission and expected approval milestones to the product release plan.
checklist.done: the change record shows a per-state earliest-use date and every Compact component is blocked in the release plan until approval.

checklist.step: Re-run affected determinations within 30 days of any Compact membership or standard change
actions: Subscribe to IIPRC Filing Information Notices and the membership announcement feed, and log the receipt date of each notice.
Within 30 days of notification of a new member state, a withdrawal, or an adopted or amended Uniform Standard, list every open determination and approved product the change touches.
Re-run the state selection and the standard mapping for those products and record whether the existing approval extends to the new member state or a new filing is required.
Record the re-determination outcome and date on each affected log row and escalate any product that has lost coverage to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: every membership or standard change has a dated re-determination completed within 30 days of notification for all affected products.

testing.step: Build the population of product components that went live in the quarter
actions: Extract from the policy admin form master and rate table change log every life, annuity, LTC and DI component with an effective date inside the quarter, by writing company and state.
Add illustration engine and rating engine configuration releases so system-only changes cannot hide from the population.
Reconcile the extract row count to the quarterly product release notes and resolve every difference before sampling.
Have the extractor sign the population as complete with the extract date and query used.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to release records and signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile every live component to a determination that pre-dates it
actions: Match each population row to a Filing Determination Log row on change id plus form number and edition date.
Confirm the determination decision date is earlier than the component's effective date in each state.
List unmatched components and late determinations as automatic exceptions with no judgement applied.
Quantify the unmatched population as a percentage and carry it into the conclusion.
testing.done: every population row is matched to a pre-dated determination or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample across paths and product families
actions: Take 100% of rows whose determination chose STATE-BY-STATE or MIX AND MATCH.
Take 25 rows at random using a seeded, reproducible selection from the remaining population, with a minimum of 40 rows in total and at least 5 rows from each of life, annuity, LTC and DI.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
Include every component effective in the representative state Arizona in the sample.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, stratified by product family and covers all non-Compact path rows.

testing.step: Re-perform the Uniform Standard mapping independently
actions: For each sampled component, open the Uniform Standards library on insurancecompact.org as of the determination date and reach your own mapping conclusion before reading the worksheet.
Compare your standard title, adoption date and section numbers to the recorded mapping; treat 'right standard, wrong section' as an exception.
Confirm the standard captured in the determination folder is the version in force on the determination date, not a later amendment.
Screenshot the standard page relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled component has an independent mapping conclusion and a captured, date-correct source page.

testing.step: Verify the opt-out and state-specific requirement checks
actions: For each sampled component, re-read the Compact opt-out record as of the determination date for every mapped standard.
Confirm any opted-out state was excluded from the Compact selection and picked up on the state-by-state tab.
Pull the state-specific requirements chart entries for three sampled states including Arizona and confirm each listed requirement is carried in the form's variable bracketing.
Treat a missing fraud warning or free-look variation as a fail, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: opt-out exclusions and state-specific requirements are verified against the source charts for every sampled component.

testing.step: Confirm registration and member-state licensure supporting the state selection
actions: Confirm the writing company's IIPRC registration was current on each sampled determination date.
For 10 sampled state selections, obtain the certificate of authority evidence for the writing company in that member state and check it pre-dates the selection.
Flag any state selected on a Compact filing where the company was not licensed as a reportable breach.
Record registration expiry dates and licensure references in the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled state selection is supported by current registration and pre-dated licensure evidence.

testing.step: Trace each Compact-path component to a real SERFF Compact filing
actions: In SERFF Filing Access set the state to the Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Commission and search each recorded SERFF tracking number.
Confirm the filing exists for the right company, product type, form number and edition date, and that the Compact Filing Information tab lists the states recorded on the determination.
Compare the submission date and disposition date to the component's effective date in each state.
Where reuse of a prior approval was claimed, open that prior filing and confirm the approved edition is genuinely the edition in use.
Capture the SERFF filing detail screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: every Compact-path component traces to a real Compact filing whose state selection matches the determination.

testing.step: Recompute the submission-date maths and the 30-day membership refresh
actions: For 10 sampled Compact rows recompute latest submission date = target effective date minus (60-day review + 30-day objection buffer + implementation lead) and compare to the actual submission date.
Identify every membership or Uniform Standard change notified during the quarter and confirm a re-determination was completed within 30 days of the notification date.
Check that any product losing coverage from a membership change was pulled from sale in that jurisdiction on the day coverage lapsed.
Log each day-count miss with the number of days late.
testing.done: submission-date maths reconciles and every membership or standard notification has a re-determination inside 30 days.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception carrying change id, form number, state, what was missed and the compliance impact.
Assign a root cause — intake missed the component, wrong Uniform Standard, stale member roster, opt-out not checked, timeline crushed — and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any component used in a member state without approval, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for undetermined components and incorrect standard mappings.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the evidence references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored none of the sampled determinations, sign the workpaper with the review date.
Report results and open breaches to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper under REG-016-C01.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Open the package checklist driven by the mapped Uniform Standard
actions: Take the closed determination row from REG-016-C01 and read off the Uniform Standard, sections and state selection.

Open the Uniform Standard on insurancecompact.org and transcribe every submission requirement it lists — scope, format, required provisions, prohibited provisions, disclosure and variability rules — into a package checklist, one line per requirement.
Add the Compact Product Filing Rule submission items: Statement of Intent, filing description, certifications, Statement of Variability, and rate schedule where applicable.
Name an owner and a due date for each checklist line and publish the checklist to Product Development, Pricing and Legal.
checklist.done: a per-requirement package checklist exists with an owner and due date on every line.

checklist.step: Collect print-ready forms with correct numbering and edition dates
actions: Request from Product Development the final policy or contract form, application, riders, endorsements and schedule pages as print-ready PDFs with the form number and edition date on every page.
Confirm the form number and edition date match the determination row exactly, character for character, and reject any file still watermarked DRAFT.
Check each PDF is text-searchable and within the SERFF per-attachment size limit, splitting oversized exhibits rather than compressing text to illegibility.
Produce a side-by-side redline against the previously approved edition for every revised form and file it with the package.
checklist.done: the form set is print-ready, correctly numbered and dated, text-searchable, and each revised form has a redline.

checklist.step: Bracket the variables and write the Statement of Variability
actions: Bracket every item intended to vary — issue ages, benefit amounts, company officer signatures, addresses, state-specific notices — using square brackets in the filed form text.

Write a Statement of Variability entry for each bracketed item giving the range or list of permitted values, the conditions under which each value is used, and a statement that variability will not be used to make the form less favourable to the consumer.
Confirm no bracketed range breaches a minimum or maximum fixed by the mapped Uniform Standard, checking each range against the standard's section text.
Fold in the state-specific requirement list from the determination so each member state's fraud warning, free-look and notice wording appears as a bracketed variation.
checklist.done: every bracket in the filed forms has a Statement of Variability entry within the Uniform Standard's limits.

checklist.step: Run and certify the readability score
actions: Run the Flesch reading ease score over each filed form using the scoring method the Uniform Standard prescribes, excluding the permitted exclusions such as defined terms and captions.
Confirm each score meets the minimum the standard requires and re-write and re-score any form that falls short rather than filing under score.
Print the score sheet showing the score, word count and exclusions applied for each form.
Have an officer sign the readability certification naming each form number and edition date and its score.
checklist.done: every filed form has a passing readability score sheet and a signed readability certification.

checklist.step: Draft the Statement of Intent and the filing description
actions: Write the filing description stating what the product is, whether it is new or a revision, what changed against the prior approved edition, and how each component maps to the Uniform Standard sections.
State plainly whether any component is being combined with a state-approved component under the Mix and Match operating procedure and name that component and its state approval.
List the member states selected and note any member state deliberately excluded, with the reason from the determination.
Have the Insurance Product Manager confirm the description matches the product actually being launched.
checklist.done: a filing description exists that names every component, the standard mapping, the state selection and any mix-and-match combination.

checklist.step: Assemble the actuarial memorandum and rate schedule for LTC and DI components
actions: Export the proposed rate schedule by issue age, benefit period, elimination period and inflation option from the actuarial model, naming the model version and valuation date.

Write the actuarial memorandum covering pricing assumptions (morbidity, mortality, lapse, interest), the anticipated lifetime loss ratio demonstration, the margin for moderately adverse experience, and a reserve basis statement.
For an LTC rate increase, add the rate increase justification, the actual-to-expected experience exhibit, and the required policyholder disclosure text.
Have a qualified actuary sign the actuarial certification naming the standards of practice relied on, and file the signed page with the memorandum.
checklist.done: the actuarial memorandum, rate schedule and signed actuarial certification are complete for every LTC and DI component.

checklist.step: Reconcile the rate schedule to the illustration and rating configuration
actions: Compare the rate schedule being filed to the rate tables loaded into the rating and illustration configuration for the same product, cell by cell for a sample of at least 30 rating cells.
Resolve every difference before filing — the filed rates and the rates the system will charge must be identical.
Record the reconciliation, the cells tested and the sign-off date, and send it to the Product Filing Specialist for the package folder.
Freeze the rate tables so no change lands between reconciliation and submission.
checklist.done: the filed rate schedule reconciles cell for cell to the frozen rating configuration with a dated sign-off.

checklist.step: Prepare the certifications the Compact requires
actions: Prepare the filing compliance certification stating that the filing complies with the applicable Uniform Standards, signed by an officer with authority to bind the insurer.
Prepare the third-party filer authorization where an outside filer submits on the company's behalf, naming the filer and the scope of authority.
Confirm each certification names the exact form numbers and edition dates in the package and carries a date on or before the submission date.
Keep the wet-signed or e-signed originals in the legal file and place the executed PDFs in the package folder.
checklist.done: every required certification is executed, correctly scoped to the filed forms, and dated on or before submission.

checklist.step: Confirm the Compact product coding and filing fees
actions: Select the Compact product type and TOI/Sub-TOI codes that match the product family and confirm they are the codes the Commission accepts for that Uniform Standard.
Compute the Compact filing fee from the current fee schedule based on the number of product components being filed, and add the per-state filing fees for each selected member state that charges one.
Confirm the writing company's annual Compact registration fee is paid and not lapsing before the expected approval date.
Send the fee total and the EFT payment instruction to Finance and record the payment reference on the package cover sheet.
checklist.done: product coding is confirmed and the total Compact plus per-state fee is computed with a payment reference on the cover sheet.

checklist.step: Assemble the package in the Compact's required order
actions: Build the folder in submission order: cover letter, filing description, form set, redlines, Statement of Variability, certifications, readability score sheets, actuarial memorandum and rate schedule, state-specific inserts.
Name every file <form number>-<edition date>-<document type>.pdf so the Commission reviewer can navigate without opening files.
Cross-tick each package checklist line against the file that satisfies it and leave no unticked line.
Lock the folder to read-only once complete and record the package version.
checklist.done: a locked, ordered, consistently named package satisfies every checklist line.

checklist.step: Run the four-eyes package QC before submission
actions: Re-read the Uniform Standard's required and prohibited provisions and confirm each required provision appears in the form text at a named page, and no prohibited provision appears anywhere.
Check every bracket in the forms has a Statement of Variability entry and every Statement of Variability entry maps to a bracket in the forms.
Confirm the form numbers, edition dates and state selection agree across the determination row, the certifications, the filing description and the file names.
Log every defect found on the QC sheet with the owner and a fix-by date, and re-QC after the fixes land.
Sign the QC sheet as passed only when the defect list is empty.
checklist.done: a signed QC sheet shows every required provision located, every bracket matched and no open defects.

checklist.step: Prepare the state-specific attachments for the selected member states
actions: For each selected member state, attach the items its entry in the Compact state-specific requirements chart calls for — fraud warning wording, required notices, and any state transmittal.
Confirm the Arizona, Connecticut and District of Columbia entries are satisfied since those jurisdictions carry the supporting citations for this obligation.
Where a state requires a filing fee remitted separately, note the amount and the remittance method against that state.
List the states and their attachments on the package cover sheet so nothing is discovered mid-review.
checklist.done: every selected member state has its chart-required attachments present and listed on the cover sheet.

checklist.step: Get the business and actuarial sign-offs on the final package
actions: Circulate the locked package to Product Development, Pricing, Legal and Compliance for final sign-off with a stated 3-business-day turnaround.
Confirm in writing that the forms in the package are the forms the business will issue and the rates are the rates it will charge.
Record each sign-off name, role and date on the package cover sheet.
Hold submission until every sign-off is recorded — a missing sign-off is not a submission risk to be accepted.
checklist.done: the cover sheet carries dated sign-offs from Product, Pricing, Legal and Compliance on the locked package.

checklist.step: Stage the package into SERFF and hold it for submission
actions: In SERFF create the filing against the Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Commission, select the Compact product type, and open the Compact Filing Information tab.
Load the state selection, the Form Schedule with each form number and edition date, the Rate/Rule Schedule where applicable, and the Supporting Documentation tab items.
Attach each package file to the tab item it satisfies so no document lands in a generic bucket.
Save without submitting and hand the staged filing to the submitter named in REG-016-C03.
checklist.done: the filing is staged in SERFF with every schedule and supporting documentation item populated and nothing left unattached.

checklist.step: Archive the exact package as staged
actions: Copy the locked package, the QC sheet, the sign-off cover sheet and the reconciliation into the compliance evidence repository under the product and target effective date.
Apply the 7-year-from-withdrawal retention label so the package survives product sunset.
Index the record by form number, edition date and writing company so it can be retrieved without knowing the SERFF tracking number.
Record the repository reference on the determination log row.
checklist.done: the staged package is archived, retention-labelled and retrievable by form number and edition date.

testing.step: Build the population of Compact packages submitted in the quarter
actions: In SERFF export the list of filings submitted to the Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Commission in the quarter for every writing company, with tracking number, product type, submission date and status.
Reconcile the export to the filing tracker's package register and resolve any package that exists in one and not the other.
Split the population by product family and by whether the filing later drew a Commission objection.
Sign the population as complete with the export date and filter criteria.
testing.done: the SERFF-derived population reconciles to the package register and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile each submitted package to a passed QC sheet
actions: Match every population row to a QC sheet signed as passed and to a cover sheet carrying the four business sign-offs.
Confirm the QC sign-off date is on or before the SERFF submission date.
List packages submitted with no QC sheet, an unsigned QC sheet or a QC sheet dated after submission as automatic exceptions.
Quantify the proportion of the population submitted without completed QC.
testing.done: every submitted package matches a pre-dated, signed QC sheet or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample weighted to objected filings
actions: Take 100% of packages that received a Commission objection citing missing or non-conforming documentation.
Take 20 further packages at random using a seeded, reproducible selection, with at least 3 LTC or DI packages so actuarial content is tested.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
State the sample coverage as a percentage of the quarter's packages.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all objected packages and includes actuarial-bearing filings.

testing.step: Re-perform the Uniform Standard completeness check on the sample
actions: For each sampled package open the Uniform Standard in force at submission and build your own requirement list before reading the package checklist.
Locate each required provision in the filed form text and record the form number and page; record any required provision you cannot find as a fail.
Scan the filed forms for provisions the standard prohibits and record any hit as a fail.
Compare your requirement list to the package checklist and note any requirement the checklist omitted.
testing.done: each sampled package has an independent requirement list with every provision located or recorded as a fail.

testing.step: Test the Statement of Variability against the filed brackets
actions: For each sampled package, list every bracketed item in the filed forms and every Statement of Variability entry, and reconcile the two lists in both directions.
Check each stated range against the minimum or maximum fixed by the Uniform Standard and record any range that exceeds it.
Confirm the state-specific variations for at least three selected member states including Arizona appear as bracketed alternatives.
Record unmatched brackets and out-of-range values as exceptions with the form number and page.
testing.done: brackets and Statement of Variability entries reconcile both ways and every range sits inside the standard's limits.

testing.step: Re-score readability and verify the certifications
actions: Re-run the Flesch score on two forms per sampled package using the standard's prescribed method and compare to the filed score sheet.
Treat a difference that moves a form below the required minimum as a fail; a difference within tolerance is logged as a scoring-method observation.
Confirm each certification names the exact form numbers and edition dates filed, is signed by an authorised officer, and is dated on or before submission.
Confirm third-party filer authorizations exist where an outside filer submitted.
testing.done: re-scored readability agrees with the filed score sheets and every certification is correctly scoped, signed and dated.

testing.step: Re-perform the actuarial memorandum and rate reconciliation for LTC and DI
actions: For each sampled LTC or DI package, recompute the anticipated lifetime loss ratio from the filed assumptions and compare to the memorandum's stated figure.
Confirm the memorandum names the pricing assumptions, the margin for moderately adverse experience and the standards of practice relied on, and carries a signed actuarial certification.
Re-run the rate reconciliation on 30 rating cells against the production rating configuration and record any cell where the filed rate and the charged rate differ.
Escalate any charged rate that differs from a filed rate as a reportable breach rather than a test exception.
testing.done: the loss ratio recomputes to the memorandum, the certification is signed, and filed rates equal charged rates on every tested cell.

testing.step: Analyse Commission objections for package-quality root cause
actions: Open each objection letter on the sampled filings in SERFF and classify what the Commission asked for — missing document, non-conforming provision, variability question, actuarial question, coding error.
Trace each objection back to the QC sheet and determine whether QC should have caught it.
Compute the objection rate per 100 packages and the share attributable to preventable completeness defects.
Compare the current quarter's rate to the prior two quarters and state the trend.
testing.done: every sampled objection is classified, traced to QC, and the preventable objection rate is computed and trended.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the SERFF tracking number, form number, defect type and regulatory impact.
Assign a root cause — checklist not built from the standard, bracket without a Statement of Variability entry, certification scoped to the wrong edition, rate table drift after freeze — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and require a package-checklist template update where the defect could recur.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a template fix where applicable.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compare the completeness fail count and the objection rate to the stated thresholds, including the 10% objection escalation trigger.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who assembled and certified none of the sampled packages, sign the workpaper with the review date.
File the workpaper under REG-016-C02 and report findings to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, objection rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Validate the staged filing against the determination before submitting
actions: Open the staged SERFF filing against the Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Commission and place the determination row beside it.
Confirm writing company, NAIC company code, Compact product type and TOI/Sub-TOI agree with the determination exactly.
Confirm every form number and edition date on the Form Schedule matches the package and the certifications.
Reject the filing back to package assembly if any field disagrees rather than correcting it in SERFF without a package update.
checklist.done: company, product coding, forms and editions in SERFF agree with the determination and the certified package.

checklist.step: Set and double-check the member state selection
actions: On the Compact Filing Information tab select each member state from the determination's state selection list, including Illinois as the representative jurisdiction for this obligation.
Confirm every selected state is a current Compact member on the dated roster snapshot and that the writing company is licensed there.
Confirm no state excluded for an opt-out or a licensure gap has been selected.
Screen-capture the completed state selection into the filing folder before submission — this is the evidence that the single filing covers the states claimed.
checklist.done: the state selection screen capture matches the determination list state for state, with no opted-out or unlicensed state selected.

checklist.step: Populate the Form Schedule and Rate/Rule Schedule
actions: Add one Form Schedule row per filed form with form number, edition date, form name, form type (policy, application, rider, endorsement, schedule page), action (new or revised) and the previous filing reference for revisions.
Attach the print-ready PDF to its own schedule row and attach the redline to the corresponding revised row.
Populate the Rate/Rule Schedule for LTC and DI filings with the rate schedule and the actuarial memorandum attached to their own rows.
Leave no schedule row without an attachment and no attachment sitting outside a schedule row.
checklist.done: every form and rate document sits on its own schedule row with the correct action code and attachment.

checklist.step: Populate the Supporting Documentation tab
actions: Attach the filing description, Statement of Variability, readability certification, filing compliance certification and third-party filer authorization each to its named Supporting Documentation item.
Attach the state-specific requirement documents for each selected member state to the item the Compact instructions specify.
Use the bypass option only where the item genuinely does not apply and type the reason into the bypass explanation — never bypass silently.
Re-read the tab top to bottom and confirm no item is left unsatisfied and unexplained.
checklist.done: every Supporting Documentation item is satisfied by an attachment or carries a written bypass reason.

checklist.step: Remit the Compact and per-state filing fees
actions: Enter the Compact filing fee computed from the current fee schedule by component count, plus the per-state fee for each selected member state that charges one.
Set the EFT payment method against the company's SERFF payment profile and confirm the account has funds cleared with Treasury before submission.
Check the fee total in SERFF equals the total on the package cover sheet and resolve any difference before submitting.
Record the EFT reference and the fee total on the filing tracker row.
checklist.done: fees are entered, funded and reconciled to the cover sheet with an EFT reference recorded.

checklist.step: Submit the filing and capture the receipt
actions: Run the SERFF submission validation and clear every error and warning it returns.
Submit the filing to the Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Commission and record the timestamp.
Copy the SERFF tracking number and the company tracking number onto the determination log row and the product change record.
Save the submission confirmation and the filing-at-a-glance page as dated PDFs into the filing folder.
checklist.done: the filing is submitted, the SERFF tracking number is recorded on the log, and a dated submission receipt is filed.

checklist.step: Confirm Compact acknowledgement and assigned reviewer
actions: Check the filing status moves from Submitted to Assigned or Under Review and note the Commission reviewer named on the filing.
If no acknowledgement appears within 1 business day, contact the IIPRC Office through SERFF Filing Correspondence and log the contact.
Record the acknowledgement date as day 0 of the Compact review period on the tracker row.
Compute and record the expected disposition date at 60 days from acknowledgement.
checklist.done: acknowledgement is captured with the reviewer name, review-period day 0 and the expected disposition date recorded.

checklist.step: Open the tracker row and set the review-period reminders
actions: Create the tracking row with SERFF tracking number, product, forms, state selection, submission date, expected disposition date and target effective date.
Set reminders at day 15, day 30 and day 50 of the review period, and a hard alert at day 60 if no disposition is recorded.
Link the row to the filing folder and to the product change record so the release gate can read the status.
Set the row owner to the submitting specialist with the Regulatory Affairs Manager as escalation.
checklist.done: an owned tracker row exists with the full identifiers, linked evidence and day-15/30/50/60 reminders armed.

checklist.step: Run the weekly Compact filing status review
actions: Pull the open Compact filing list from the tracker every Monday, sorted by days elapsed in the review period.
Review each filing over day 30 with its owner and record what is outstanding — Commission review, an open objection, or an internal response in preparation.
Compare the expected disposition date to the target effective date for each filing and flag those where approval will land too late.
Minute the decisions and the owners and publish the list to the Insurance Product Manager for release planning.
checklist.done: a weekly minuted review covers every open filing, with a flag on every filing whose approval will miss the target date.

checklist.step: Handle filings returned or rejected for incompleteness
actions: Read the Commission's reason for return or rejection on the filing correspondence and classify it as a coding error, missing document, wrong state selection or ineligible product.
Fix the defect in the package, re-run the QC sheet on the affected checklist lines, and note the fix on the tracker row.
Re-submit or amend as the Commission's instruction directs, and record the new tracking number where a fresh filing is required.
Raise a tracker exception with the root cause so the package checklist can be corrected for the next filing.
checklist.done: every returned filing has a classified cause, a re-QC-ed fix, a resubmission reference and a logged exception.

checklist.step: Record the disposition and its scope when it arrives
actions: Open the Disposition on the SERFF filing and read the disposition status, the disposition date and the approval letter attached to it.
Confirm the disposition covers every form number and edition date submitted and every member state selected, and list any state the Commission excluded.
Download the approval letter and the filing-at-a-glance page as dated PDFs into the filing folder.
Write the disposition status, date and covered state list onto the tracker row and the determination log row.
checklist.done: the disposition, its date and the exact list of covered forms and states are recorded and evidenced by the downloaded letter.

checklist.step: Reconcile the approved scope back to the state selection
actions: Compare the approved state list on the disposition to the state selection screen capture taken at submission, state by state.
Compare the approved form numbers and edition dates to the Form Schedule as submitted.
Raise an exception where a state or form was submitted but not approved, and route those states to the state-by-state filing path.
Confirm Illinois specifically is covered where the product is to be sold there, since Illinois carries the representative citation for this obligation.
checklist.done: approved states and forms reconcile to the submission, and every gap is routed to an alternative filing path.

checklist.step: Publish the disposition to the release gate
actions: Attach the approval letter to the product change record and set the per-state earliest-use dates from the disposition date.
Release the pre-use gate only for the states and forms named in the disposition and leave it set for everything else.
Notify Distribution and Policy Administration of the approved state list and the earliest-use dates in writing.
Record the notification date and recipients on the change record.
checklist.done: the gate is released only for approved states and forms, with dated notifications to Distribution and Policy Administration.

checklist.step: Chase filings that pass the expected disposition date
actions: At day 60 with no disposition, send a status enquiry to the assigned Commission reviewer through SERFF Filing Correspondence and log the date sent.
Escalate to the IIPRC Office if there is no reply within 5 business days and record the escalation.
Tell the Insurance Product Manager to re-plan the launch date rather than assume approval, since no deemer substitutes for Compact approval.
Keep the tracker row open and reported weekly until a disposition is recorded.
checklist.done: every filing past day 60 has a logged enquiry, an escalation where unanswered, and a re-planned launch date.

checklist.step: Archive the submission and disposition evidence
actions: File the submission receipt, state selection capture, fee remittance reference, correspondence thread and approval letter under the product and SERFF tracking number.
Apply the 7-year-from-withdrawal retention label to the filing record.
Index the record by SERFF tracking number, form number, writing company and member state.
Record the repository reference on the tracker row and close the row.
checklist.done: the filing record is complete, retention-labelled, indexed by tracking number and state, and the tracker row is closed.

testing.step: Build the population of Compact filings for the quarter
actions: Export from SERFF every filing to the Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Commission with a submission or disposition date in the quarter, for all writing companies.
Capture tracking number, product type, submission date, status, disposition date and the selected state list for each.
Reconcile the export to the filing tracker's open and closed rows and resolve every row present in one and absent from the other.
Sign the population as complete with the export date and filter criteria.
testing.done: the SERFF export reconciles to the tracker with no unexplained rows on either side.

testing.step: Reconcile filings to determinations and to products actually in market
actions: Match each filing to its determination row on form number and edition date and confirm the determination pre-dates the submission.
Take the list of products issued in the quarter by state from policy admin and confirm each product-state pair appears on an approved Compact filing's state list or on a separate state filing.
List every product-state pair with no covering approval as an automatic exception and a candidate breach.
Quantify unmatched pairs as a percentage of issued business.
testing.done: every issued product-state pair is matched to a covering approval or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample across statuses
actions: Take 100% of filings returned, rejected or still open beyond 90 days.
Take 20 disposed filings at random using a seeded, reproducible selection, including at least 5 covering Illinois.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper.
State the sample coverage as a percentage of the quarter's filings.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all problem filings and includes Illinois-covering filings.

testing.step: Re-perform the state selection check in SERFF
actions: Open each sampled filing's Compact Filing Information tab and read the state selection as submitted.
Compare it to the determination's state list and to the state selection screen capture in the filing folder, and treat any difference as an exception.
Confirm no selected state had opted out of a mapped Uniform Standard and that the writing company held a licence in each selected state at submission.
Capture the tab into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled filing's submitted state selection is independently verified against the determination, the opt-out record and licensure.

testing.step: Trace the submission receipt, fees and identifiers
actions: For each sampled filing confirm a dated submission receipt and a Compact acknowledgement exist in the filing folder and carry the same tracking number as the SERFF record.
Recompute the Compact fee from the component count and the per-state fees from the selected states, and agree the total to the EFT remittance reference.
Confirm the company tracking number on the filing matches the product change record.
Record any missing receipt, fee difference or identifier mismatch as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled filing has a matched receipt, an agreed fee computation and consistent identifiers.

testing.step: Recompute submission timing against the latest submission date
actions: For each sampled filing recompute the latest submission date as target effective date minus (60-day review + 30-day objection buffer + implementation lead).
Compare the actual submission date and record the number of days early or late.
Count every filing submitted after its latest submission date as a fail against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Analyse late submissions by cause — package delay, actuarial delay, fee funding, business change of scope.
testing.done: submission timing is recomputed for every sampled filing with late filings counted and cause-analysed.

testing.step: Age every open filing and test the chase evidence
actions: Build an ageing of all open Compact filings in buckets of 0-30, 31-60, 61-90 and over 90 days from acknowledgement.
For every filing over 60 days confirm a logged SERFF enquiry to the assigned reviewer exists and an escalation where the enquiry went unanswered for 5 business days.
Confirm the weekly status review minutes cover every filing in the 61-90 and over-90 buckets.
Record every over-90-day filing with no disposition as a fail.
testing.done: the ageing is complete and every filing past day 60 has evidenced enquiry, escalation and weekly review coverage.

testing.step: Verify dispositions against the approved scope and the release gate
actions: Open the Disposition on each sampled approved filing and list the approved forms, edition dates and states from the approval letter.
Compare that list to the earliest-use dates and state availability configured on the product change record and in policy admin.
Identify any state or form released for use that the disposition does not cover, and treat it as a reportable breach rather than a test exception.
Capture the disposition page and the approval letter into the workpaper.
testing.done: released states and forms sit inside the approved scope for every sampled filing, with any excess reported as a breach.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the SERFF tracking number, the state or form affected and the compliance impact.
Assign a root cause — state selection error, late submission, unfunded fee, no acknowledgement chase, disposition scope not reconciled — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel for any product used in a state outside the approved scope.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compare the fail counts for uncovered product-state pairs, late submissions and over-90-day open filings to the zero-tolerance thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who submitted and tracked none of the sampled filings, sign the workpaper with the review date.
File the workpaper under REG-016-C03 and report findings and breaches to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, fail counts and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Arm the pre-use gate the moment the determination closes
actions: Create the form-master record for each Compact component with status BLOCKED and no state availability rows.
Set the rate table effective date to a placeholder in the future so it cannot be picked up by quoting before approval.
Link the form-master record to the SERFF tracking number and the determination log row so the gate can be reconciled to a filing.
Confirm with the Insurance Product Manager in writing that no distribution or marketing material for the form has been released.
checklist.done: every Compact component exists in policy admin as BLOCKED with no state availability and a linked SERFF tracking number.

checklist.step: Publish the per-state gate status to the launch plan
actions: Build the launch matrix listing every target member state against form number, filing status and expected approval date.
Mark every state RED until an approval is recorded and publish the matrix to Distribution, Marketing and Contact Centre leadership weekly.
State plainly in the matrix that no Compact filing carries a deemer — silence from the Commission never authorises use.
Record acknowledgement from each distribution channel lead that they will not solicit on a RED state.
checklist.done: a weekly launch matrix shows every state RED until approval with dated acknowledgement from each channel lead.

checklist.step: Block the sales, illustration and quoting front ends
actions: Suppress the new form and its riders from the illustration engine product list for every state until availability is opened.
Suppress the product from the quoting front end and the agent portal product picker for the same state set.
Add a hard validation that rejects a new business submission naming a BLOCKED form number with a message naming the awaiting-approval status.
Test the block in the pre-production environment for three states including Arkansas and record the test evidence.
checklist.done: illustration, quoting and new business submission all reject the blocked form in every state, evidenced by a pre-production test.

checklist.step: Read the disposition and extract the approved scope
actions: Open the Compact filing's Disposition in SERFF and download the approval letter.
List from the letter every approved form number and edition date and every member state the approval covers, including whether Arkansas is inside or outside the approved list.
Note the Commission's approval date, which is the earliest date the product may be used in a covered state.
Send the approved scope table to the Policy Admin Ops Lead with the approval letter attached.
checklist.done: an approved scope table naming forms, editions, states and the approval date is issued with the approval letter attached.

checklist.step: Verify no state was silently dropped from the approval
actions: Compare the approved state list to the state selection screen capture taken at submission, state by state.
For each state on the submission but not the approval, read the filing correspondence to find why and record the reason.
Keep the gate CLOSED for every unapproved state and route it to the state-by-state filing path or a follow-on Compact filing.
Escalate to the Regulatory Affairs Manager any state dropped without a written reason in the correspondence.
checklist.done: every submitted state is either covered by the approval or has a written reason and a closed gate.

checklist.step: Set the per-state earliest-use dates from the approval
actions: For each approved state create the state availability row with an effective-from date equal to the Commission approval date, never earlier.
Where the business wants a later coordinated launch date, set the availability date later — never bring it forward to a build date or a target date.
Set the rate table effective date to the same date so rates cannot be applied before the form is available.
Have a second operator check the dates against the approval letter and initial the change record.
checklist.done: each approved state carries an availability and rate effective date on or after the approval date, checked by a second operator.

checklist.step: Release the gate only for the approved form editions
actions: Move the form-master status from BLOCKED to ACTIVE only for form numbers and edition dates named in the approval letter.
Leave every unapproved rider, endorsement and schedule page BLOCKED even where the base contract is approved.
Confirm the approved edition date printed on the issued form output matches the approved edition character for character.
Record the release in the change record with the approval letter reference and the releaser's name and date.
checklist.done: only approved form numbers and edition dates are ACTIVE, and the printed edition date matches the approval.

checklist.step: Prove the gate with a controlled pre-release test
actions: Attempt to issue a test policy in an approved state with an issue date one day before the approval date and confirm the system rejects it.
Attempt to issue a test policy in an unapproved state and confirm the system rejects it.
Issue a test policy in an approved state on the approval date and confirm the correct form edition and rate table are applied.
File the three test results with screenshots in the release evidence folder and require them before production release.
checklist.done: the gate provably rejects pre-approval and unapproved-state issues and applies the correct edition on the approval date.

checklist.step: Turn on the daily use-before-approval exception report
actions: Build a daily report joining issued policies to the approved form-state-date table and returning any policy whose issue date precedes the state's approval date.
Include policy number, form number, edition date, state, issue date, approval date and days early on every exception row.
Route the report to the Policy Admin Ops Lead and the Compliance Analyst each morning, with an explicit zero-exception statement on clean days.
Alert the Head of Compliance automatically on any non-zero day.
checklist.done: a daily exception report runs, is distributed with a zero statement on clean days, and auto-alerts on any exception.

checklist.step: Notify distribution the day a state opens
actions: Send the approved-state list and earliest-use dates to the field, the agent portal and the contact centre on the day the gate is released.
Update the agent portal product availability page and the contact centre knowledge article with the same dates.
Withdraw any pre-launch marketing material that named a state still awaiting approval.
Record the notification date, channels and recipients on the product change record.
checklist.done: distribution channels carry the approved state list and earliest-use dates from the release date, with a dated record.

checklist.step: Control gate overrides tightly
actions: Require any request to open a state before a recorded approval to be raised in writing with the business reason and the regulatory analysis.
Refuse any override that would put a Compact form into use in a member state before the Commission approval date — there is no deemer to rely on.
Where an override is granted for a non-Compact path (for example the state was moved to a state filing and approved there), record the state approval reference on the override.
Log every override request, decision, approver and date in the release gate record.
checklist.done: every override request has a written decision, an approver and a named alternative approval reference, with no pre-approval Compact use permitted.

checklist.step: Re-check gate coverage when Compact membership changes
actions: On notification that a jurisdiction has joined or left the Compact, list every ACTIVE Compact form and its state availability rows.
For a new member state, confirm whether an existing approval extends to it or a new filing is needed, and keep the state BLOCKED until that is resolved.
For a withdrawing jurisdiction, close availability on the date its withdrawal takes effect and route the state to a state filing.
Complete the re-check within 30 days of the membership notification and record the outcome per form.
checklist.done: every membership change has a per-form gate re-check completed within 30 days of notification.

checklist.step: Run the post-release verification sweep
actions: Two weeks after each release, extract every policy issued on the new form by state and compare the earliest issue date per state to the approval date.
Check the issued document image shows the approved form number and edition date, on a sample of five policies per state.
Confirm the rate applied on those policies matches the filed rate schedule for LTC and DI forms.
Record the sweep result on the release gate record and close the release only when it is clean.
checklist.done: a two-week sweep shows the earliest issue date on or after approval in every state and correct editions and rates on the sampled policies.

checklist.step: Handle a use-before-approval breach immediately
actions: On any exception, freeze new issues on the affected form and state within the same business day and record the freeze time.
List every affected policy with policy number, issue date, state and premium, and quantify the exposure.
Work with Regulatory Counsel on the remedy — reissue on an approved edition, endorse, or self-report to the Commission and the member state.
Open a tracker issue with root cause, owner and remediation date and report it to the Head of Compliance the same day.
checklist.done: the form is frozen, affected policies are listed and quantified, and a counsel-cleared remedy with a self-report decision is recorded.

checklist.step: Archive the release gate record
actions: File the gate armed date, approval letter, per-state earliest-use table, second-operator check, QA gate test evidence, override log and sweep result under the product and form number.
Apply the 7-year-from-withdrawal retention label.
Index the record by form number, edition date and member state so an examiner question about a single state can be answered without opening the whole product file.
Record the repository reference on the determination log row.
checklist.done: a complete release gate record is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by form number and state.

testing.step: Build the population of policies issued on Compact forms
actions: Extract every policy and contract issued in the quarter on a Compact-filed form with policy number, form number, edition date, writing company, state and issue date.
Add reinstatements, conversions and rider additions since they can apply a form edition outside the original issue.
Reconcile the count and premium to the quarterly new business report and resolve any difference before testing.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date and query used.
testing.done: the issued-policy population is reconciled to the new business report and signed as complete.

testing.step: Join the population to the approved form-state-date table
actions: Build the approved table independently from the SERFF dispositions rather than from policy admin configuration — form number, edition date, state, approval date.
Join each issued policy on form number, edition date and state and compute days between approval date and issue date.
List every policy with a negative day count, and every policy with no matching approval row at all, as automatic exceptions.
Quantify exceptions by count, premium and number of states affected.
testing.done: every issued policy is matched to an independently built approval row or listed as an exception with the day count.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of policies and states
actions: Take 100% of exception policies from the join.
Take the first-issued policy in each state for every form released in the quarter, since that policy proves the gate held.
Take 20 further policies at random using a seeded, reproducible selection, including at least 3 issued in Arkansas.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and includes every exception and every state-level first-issue policy.

testing.step: Re-perform the approval-date lookup in SERFF
actions: For each sampled policy open the Compact filing in SERFF Filing Access and read the disposition date and the approved state list from the approval letter.
Confirm the policy's state appears on the approval and the issue date is on or after the disposition date.
Treat reliance on any deemer, expiry of the 60-day review, or an internal target date as an automatic fail — only the Commission approval authorises use.
Capture the disposition page into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled policy is independently confirmed against the SERFF approval date and approved state list.

testing.step: Verify the issued document carries the approved edition
actions: Pull the issued policy document image for each sampled policy from the document repository.
Read the form number and edition date printed in the footer of the contract, the application and each rider.
Compare them character for character to the approval letter and record any mismatch, including an unapproved rider attached to an approved contract.
Confirm the state-specific fraud warning and free-look wording required for that member state appears in the issued document.
testing.done: every sampled issued document carries only approved form numbers and edition dates and the required state-specific wording.

testing.step: Re-perform the gate controls in the configuration
actions: Read the state availability effective-from date and the rate table effective date configured for each sampled form and state.
Confirm both equal or post-date the approval date and that no row was backdated after release.
Read the configuration change history and confirm a second-operator check was recorded on each dating change.
Re-run the QA gate test in a test environment for one sampled form and confirm a pre-approval issue is still rejected today.
testing.done: configured availability and rate dates post-date approval, carry a second-operator check, and the gate still rejects a pre-approval issue.

testing.step: Test every gate override and its authority
actions: List every override recorded in the release gate record during the quarter.
Confirm each carries a written business reason, a regulatory analysis and a Head of Compliance approval dated before the state opened.
Confirm no override opened a Compact form in a member state before the Commission approval date; any that did is a reportable breach.
Where an override relied on a separate state approval, trace that state approval in SERFF and confirm it pre-dates the opening.
testing.done: every override has documented authority and a traced alternative approval, with no pre-approval Compact use permitted.

testing.step: Recompute the membership-change re-check and its 30-day clock
actions: List every Compact membership change notified during the quarter with its notification date and effective date.
Confirm a per-form gate re-check was completed within 30 days of each notification and record the actual day count.
For a jurisdiction that withdrew, confirm state availability was closed on the effective date and no policy was issued there afterwards.
For a jurisdiction that joined, confirm it stayed BLOCKED until a covering approval was recorded.
testing.done: every membership change has a re-check inside 30 days with availability opened or closed on the correct date.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with policy numbers, form number, state, days early and premium exposure.
Assign a root cause — availability date set from the target date, unapproved rider left ACTIVE, override without authority, membership change missed — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel for every use-before-approval policy.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a self-report decision where use preceded approval.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compare the count of pre-approval issues and unauthorised overrides to the zero-tolerance threshold and state the premium exposure.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who configured no gate and approved no override, sign the workpaper with the review date.
File the workpaper under REG-016-C04 and report every use-before-approval breach to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, breach count, premium exposure and committee reporting date exists in the repository.
