checklist.step: Maintain the IIPRC member jurisdiction roster as reference data
actions: Hold the member roster as a governed reference list with one row per jurisdiction carrying join date, withdrawal date if any, and the source announcement reference.
Refresh the roster from insurancecompact.org monthly and within 30 days of any notified membership change, recording the retrieval date on every refresh.
Publish the roster to policy admin, the illustration engine and the filing tracker through the standard reference-data distribution rather than by spreadsheet.
Alert the Policy Admin Ops Lead and Product Compliance on any row that changes.
checklist.done: the roster is governed, dated, refreshed within 30 days of any change, and distributed to consuming systems automatically.

checklist.step: Raise the change ticket from the approval letter
actions: Open a change ticket naming the SERFF tracking number, the Commission approval date and the product change record.
Attach the approval letter and paste the approved form numbers, edition dates and member states into the ticket as the authoritative scope.
State in the ticket that configuration may not exceed that scope and that any additional state requires its own approval.
Set the required-by date to the earliest-use date minus the UAT and release lead time.
checklist.done: a change ticket carries the approval letter, the approved scope verbatim and a required-by date ahead of the earliest-use date.

checklist.step: Build the form master entries for the approved editions
actions: Create or version each form master record with the exact approved form number and edition date, the form type and its attachment rules to the base contract.
Load the approved PDF or composition template so the printed footer renders the approved form number and edition date.
Configure the state availability rows only for the approved member states, with effective-from equal to the approval date.
Leave every non-approved rider or schedule page out of the build entirely rather than building it inactive.
checklist.done: form master entries exist for approved editions only, with availability limited to approved states from the approval date.

checklist.step: Load the approved rate tables and rating rules
actions: Load the filed rate schedule for LTC and DI products keyed by issue age, benefit period, elimination period and inflation option, with the effective date set to the approval date.
Load the annuity and life rate or factor tables from the pricing hand-off file, naming the actuarial model version on the load record.
Configure the rating rules the Uniform Standard permits — minimum and maximum issue ages, benefit limits, substandard rating rules — from the filed form text, not from the marketing sheet.
Version the tables so the pre-approval rates remain retrievable for in-force business.
checklist.done: approved rate tables and rating rules are loaded, dated from approval, versioned, and traceable to the filed schedule.

checklist.step: Reconcile loaded rates to the filed rate schedule
actions: Extract the loaded rate table from the rating engine and place it beside the rate schedule attached to the SERFF filing.
Reconcile every cell for LTC and DI, and a stratified sample of at least 100 cells for life and annuity factor tables, covering the youngest and oldest issue ages and every benefit option.
Resolve every difference before release — a rate the system charges that was not filed is an unfiled rate.
Sign the reconciliation with the cells tested, the differences found and the resolution date, and attach it to the change ticket.
checklist.done: a signed cell-level reconciliation shows the loaded rates equal the filed rate schedule with zero unresolved differences.

checklist.step: Configure the state-specific variations the Compact leaves to the states
actions: For each approved member state configure the bracketed variations from the Statement of Variability — fraud warning wording, free-look period, required notices and disclosure inserts.
Confirm the Alabama, Connecticut and Georgia variations are configured, since those jurisdictions carry the supporting citations for this obligation.
Drive the variation selection from the state on the policy rather than from the agent's selection so it cannot be overridden at point of sale.
Render one specimen document per state and file it in the change ticket.
checklist.done: every approved state renders its own required wording automatically, evidenced by a specimen document per state.

checklist.step: Build the illustration and disclosure outputs
actions: Configure the illustration engine with the approved product, the loaded rates and the guaranteed and non-guaranteed elements as the filed form defines them.
Add the required disclosure pages the Uniform Standard calls for, including LTC rate increase history disclosures where applicable.
Confirm the illustration cannot be produced for a state without an approved availability row.
Run one illustration per product per approved state family and file the outputs in the change ticket.
checklist.done: illustrations produce only for approved states, carry the required disclosures, and match the loaded rates.

checklist.step: Update the product availability matrix consumed downstream
actions: Publish the approved form-state-edition matrix as governed reference data with the SERFF tracking number and approval date on every row.
Point the agent portal, quoting front end, contact centre knowledge base and new business workflow at that single matrix rather than local copies.
Retire any local product availability spreadsheet still in use and record its retirement in the ticket.
Set the matrix to reject any row whose state is not on the current member roster.
checklist.done: one governed availability matrix feeds every downstream channel and rejects non-member states.

checklist.step: Run UAT against the approval letter, not the build spec
actions: Write test cases directly from the approval letter — one per approved form and edition, one per approved state, and one negative case per unapproved state.
Execute new business, illustration, quote and document print for at least five approved states including Alabama.
Confirm the printed form number and edition date, the applied rate and the state-specific wording on every output.
Fail the build on any output showing an unapproved edition, an unfiled rate or a missing state notice, and re-test after the fix.
checklist.done: UAT is executed from the approval letter with passing evidence per approved state and rejection evidence per unapproved state.

checklist.step: Reconcile the configured scope to the approved scope before release
actions: Export the configured form-state-edition matrix from the change and compare it row by row to the approval letter.
List rows configured but not approved and rows approved but not configured, and require both lists to be empty before release.
Confirm every configured state is on the current member roster with a join date before the approval date.
Sign the reconciliation into the change ticket as a release precondition.
checklist.done: the configured matrix equals the approved scope exactly, with a signed reconciliation attached to the change ticket.

checklist.step: Release to production under dual control
actions: Require the change ticket to carry the approval letter, the rate reconciliation, UAT sign-off and the scope reconciliation before the change advisory board approves it.
Deploy with a second engineer verifying the effective dates on the deployed configuration against the approval date.
Record deployer, verifier, deployment timestamp and the configuration version in the change record.
Run the post-deployment smoke test on one approved and one unapproved state before declaring the change complete.
checklist.done: the release is approved with all four artefacts, deployed under dual control, and smoke-tested on an approved and an unapproved state.

checklist.step: Reflect the approval status back onto the product record
actions: Write the SERFF tracking number, approval date and approved state list onto the product master record so filing status is readable from the product, not only from the filing tracker.
Set the product's compliance status to APPROVED — COMPACT with the covered state count and the roster snapshot date.
Link the product record to the archived filing package and approval letter.
Confirm the reporting view used by the Compliance Committee picks the product up with the correct status.
checklist.done: the product record carries the Compact approval status, covered states and links to the filing evidence, and reports correctly.

checklist.step: Re-derive product availability within 30 days of any membership change
actions: On a roster change, run the impact query listing every configured form-state row affected by the joining or withdrawing jurisdiction.
For a withdrawal, schedule the availability row to close on the withdrawal effective date and notify Distribution before it lands.
For a new member, keep availability closed and raise a determination request so Product Compliance can decide whether an existing approval extends.
Complete the impact assessment and the configuration change within 30 days of the membership notification and record the dates.
checklist.done: every membership change has an impact query, a scheduled configuration change and a completion date inside 30 days.

checklist.step: Monitor configuration drift between releases
actions: Run a monthly automated comparison of the live form-state-edition matrix against the approval-derived matrix and report differences.
Investigate any row added, removed or re-dated outside a change ticket and identify who made it and when from the configuration audit log.
Raise a change incident for every unauthorised difference and back it out unless a valid approval supports it.
Report the monthly drift count to the Policy Admin Ops Lead and Compliance.
checklist.done: a monthly drift report exists, every unauthorised difference has an incident, and drift is reported to Ops and Compliance.

checklist.step: Archive the system change record
actions: File the change ticket, approval letter, configuration diff, rate reconciliation, UAT evidence, scope reconciliation and dual-control release record under the product and form number.
Apply the 7-year-from-withdrawal retention label so the configuration history survives product sunset.
Index the record by form number, edition date, state and SERFF tracking number.
Record the repository reference on the change ticket and close it.
checklist.done: a complete system change record is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by form number, state and tracking number.

testing.step: Build the population of implementations and the configured matrix
actions: Extract every change ticket in the quarter carrying a Compact approval reference, with product, form numbers, states and release date.
Extract the full live form-state-edition matrix from policy admin as at quarter end.
Reconcile the ticket list to the deployment log so no configuration change reached production without a ticket.
Sign the population as complete with the extract dates and queries used.
testing.done: the ticket population reconciles to the deployment log and the live configured matrix is captured as at quarter end.

testing.step: Reconcile the live configuration to the SERFF approval record
actions: Build the approved matrix independently from SERFF Compact dispositions — form number, edition date, state, approval date.
Full-outer-join it to the live configured matrix and list configured-not-approved rows and approved-not-configured rows.
Treat every configured-not-approved row as a fail and quantify the policies issued on it.
Investigate approved-not-configured rows as lost distribution and record them as observations.
testing.done: the two matrices are joined in full with every configured-not-approved row counted as a fail and quantified.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of implementations
actions: Take 100% of implementations that produced a configuration incident or a drift finding in the quarter.
Take 15 further implementations at random using a seeded, reproducible selection, including at least 3 LTC or DI products so rates are tested.
Include every implementation touching Alabama, Connecticut or Georgia in the sample.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all incident implementations and includes rate-bearing products and the cited states.

testing.step: Re-perform the rate load reconciliation independently
actions: Extract the production rate table for each sampled LTC or DI product and compare it cell by cell to the rate schedule attached to the SERFF filing.
Rate five specimen risks per product through the production engine and compare the premium to a hand calculation from the filed schedule.
Record any cell or premium difference with the magnitude and the number of in-force policies exposed.
Escalate any charged rate that is not a filed rate as a reportable breach rather than a test exception.
testing.done: production rates reconcile cell by cell and specimen premiums agree with hand calculations from the filed schedule.

testing.step: Verify the rendered documents and state-specific wording
actions: Render or pull one issued document per sampled product for three approved states including Alabama.
Confirm the printed form number and edition date match the approval letter exactly.
Confirm the state fraud warning, free-look wording and required notices for that state are present and match the Statement of Variability entries.
Attempt a render for one unapproved state and confirm the system refuses.
testing.done: rendered documents carry approved editions and correct state wording, and unapproved states cannot render.

testing.step: Test the currency and governance of the member roster
actions: Read the roster's last-refresh date and compare it to today and to the date of the most recent Compact membership announcement.
Compare the stored roster jurisdiction by jurisdiction to the current list published on insurancecompact.org and list every difference.
Confirm the roster is consumed by policy admin and the availability matrix by system reference rather than a manual copy.
Record any refresh gap beyond 30 days from a notified change as a fail.
testing.done: the stored roster agrees with the published list, is refreshed inside 30 days of any change, and is consumed by reference.

testing.step: Test change control and dual-control evidence
actions: For each sampled implementation confirm the change ticket carries the approval letter, the signed rate reconciliation, UAT sign-off and the scope reconciliation before change approval.
Confirm the deployer and the verifier are different named individuals and that the verifier checked effective dates against the approval date.
Trace one configuration item per sampled implementation from the approval letter through the ticket to the deployed value.
Record any release made without all four artefacts as a control failure.
testing.done: every sampled release has the four artefacts, distinct deployer and verifier, and a traced configuration item.

testing.step: Recompute the membership-change impact and its 30-day clock
actions: List every membership announcement in the quarter with its notification and effective dates.
Confirm an impact query was run and the resulting configuration change completed within 30 days of notification, and record the actual day count.
For any withdrawal confirm availability closed on the effective date and no policy issued afterwards in that jurisdiction.
For any new member confirm availability stayed closed pending a determination.
testing.done: each membership change has an evidenced impact assessment and configuration change inside 30 days with the correct dating.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an incident per exception with the form number, state, configured value, approved value and exposure.
Assign a root cause — scope taken from the build spec instead of the approval letter, rate table loaded from a draft file, stale roster, drift outside change control — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and require a back-out where an unapproved state or edition is live.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an incident, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a back-out where scope was exceeded.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compare the counts of configured-not-approved rows, rate differences and roster refresh gaps to the zero-tolerance thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who built, tested and released none of the sampled configurations, sign the workpaper with the review date.
File the workpaper under REG-016-C05 and report findings to the Compliance Committee and the change advisory board.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, fail counts and reporting dates exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Log every objection letter the day it arrives

Download the objection letter and record objection date, the Commission reviewer's name, the stated response date and the number of numbered items.
Create an objection log row per numbered item — not one row per letter — so no sub-question is lost in a long letter.
Notify the Insurance Product Manager the same day, since an objection moves the expected approval date.
checklist.done: every objection is logged the day it arrives with one row per numbered item and the stated response date recorded.

checklist.step: Triage each item and assign an owner within 48 hours
actions: Classify each item as form wording, variability, actuarial or rate, product coding, state-specific requirement, or documentation gap.

Assign the owner by classification — Policy Forms Specialist for wording, Product / Filing Actuary for rate and memorandum items, Regulatory Counsel for standard-interpretation items, Product Filing Specialist for documentation.
Set the internal draft-due date at objection day 10 and the clearance date at day 20, working back from the stated response date.
Flag any item that would change the product design and escalate it to the Insurance Product Manager immediately.
checklist.done: every objection item has a classification, a named owner and internal draft and clearance dates inside the response deadline.

checklist.step: Read the objection against the Uniform Standard section it cites
actions: Open the Uniform Standard section the reviewer cites and read it beside the filed form text the objection points at.
Decide whether the filing genuinely does not conform, or conforms but was not explained clearly, and record which on the log row.
Where the objection appears to misread the filing, draft the point of clarification with the exact page and paragraph reference rather than arguing generally.
Where the objection is right, state the required change and its knock-on effects on other forms, the Statement of Variability and the rate schedule.
checklist.done: each item records a conformance conclusion with the standard section, the form page cited and the knock-on effects listed.

checklist.step: Draft the response item by item
actions: Answer each numbered item in the reviewer's own numbering and order so nothing appears skipped.
For each item state the action taken — text amended, variability entry revised, document attached, or clarification with the standard citation supporting the original position.
Name the amended form number and edition date, and the replacement attachment, on every item that changes a document.
Never answer an item with a promise to follow up later; either answer it or request an extension explicitly.
checklist.done: a draft response answers every numbered item in order with a stated action and named amended documents.

checklist.step: Produce the amended forms and re-run the affected QC lines
actions: Amend the form text, advance the edition date where the Commission requires it, and produce a redline against the version originally filed.
Re-check the amended text against the Uniform Standard's required and prohibited provisions and re-score readability if the change is substantive.
Update the Statement of Variability for any bracket added, removed or re-ranged by the amendment.
Re-run the affected package QC checklist lines and record the re-QC on the QC sheet.
checklist.done: amended forms carry a redline, a re-checked provision list, an updated Statement of Variability and a re-QC record.

checklist.step: Clear actuarial items with the filing actuary
actions: Answer rate and memorandum items with the model output supporting the answer, naming the model version and valuation date.
Where the objection requires a rate change, rerun the loss ratio demonstration and re-issue the rate schedule with a new version reference.
Update and re-sign the actuarial certification where any certified figure or assumption changes.
Send the Pricing Actuary a re-reconciliation instruction so the rating configuration is corrected before implementation.
checklist.done: every actuarial item is answered with named model evidence and, where rates changed, a re-signed certification and re-reconciliation instruction.

checklist.step: Get Regulatory Counsel clearance before submitting
actions: Read every response item that concedes a non-conformity, changes a certified statement, or argues a standard interpretation back at the reviewer.
Confirm the response does not create an inconsistency with the filing compliance certification already on file, and amend the certification where it does.

Check the response does not commit the company to conduct in a member state it has not confirmed it can meet, with Alaska and the other supporting jurisdictions named in this obligation checked specifically.
Record the clearance name and date on the objection log row before submission.
checklist.done: counsel clearance is recorded on every item that concedes, argues or changes a certified statement, before submission.

checklist.step: Submit the response inside the stated deadline
actions: In SERFF open the objection and create the Response Letter, pasting the item-by-item response text.
Replace the superseded attachments on the Form Schedule and Rate/Rule Schedule with the amended versions so the schedules always show what is currently before the Commission.
Submit on or before the Commission's stated response date, targeting no later than day 25 of the internal 30-day standard.
Record the submission timestamp, the response letter reference and the day count on the objection log row.
checklist.done: the response is submitted before the stated date with amended schedules in place and the day count recorded.

checklist.step: Request an extension in writing when the deadline cannot be met
actions: Where the answer needs more time, send an extension request through SERFF Filing Correspondence before the stated response date, never after it.
State what is outstanding, why, and the date the response will be delivered.
Record the Commission's reply and the revised date on the objection log row and reset the internal reminders to it.
Never allow a deadline to pass in silence — an unanswered objection can lead the Commission to treat the filing as withdrawn.
checklist.done: any deadline that cannot be met has a pre-deadline written extension request and a recorded revised date.

checklist.step: Escalate at day 15 when the response is not on track
actions: Review every open objection at day 15 against its draft and clearance status.
Escalate to the item owner's manager and the Insurance Product Manager any item with no draft at day 15.
Reallocate the item where the owner cannot deliver, and record the reallocation on the log row.
Report any objection at risk of missing its stated date to the Head of Compliance the same day.
checklist.done: every objection off track at day 15 has a dated escalation, a reallocation where needed, and a Head of Compliance notification.

checklist.step: Track the follow-on objection and close only on disposition
actions: After submitting, watch the filing status for a further objection and open a new log row set for any second-round letter.
Close the objection log rows only when the filing reaches a disposition, not when the response is sent.
Where the Commission accepts an item without comment in the next letter, record that acceptance against the original item.
Report objection round counts per filing weekly so repeat rounds surface as a package-quality signal.
checklist.done: objection rows stay open until disposition, second rounds are logged separately, and round counts are reported weekly.

checklist.step: Push the amended scope back into the product and configuration record
actions: Update the product change record with every amended form number and edition date arising from the objection.
Tell the Policy Admin Ops Lead which configuration items must change before release, and confirm the change ticket is updated.
Re-plan the launch date from the revised expected approval date and communicate it to Distribution.
Confirm no build proceeds on the superseded edition.
checklist.done: the product record, the configuration ticket and the launch plan all reflect the amended editions and revised approval date.

checklist.step: Handle an objection that removes a member state
actions: Where the Commission's resolution excludes a member state from the approval, record the state, the reason and the objection item that drove it.
Route the excluded state to the state-by-state filing path and open a determination for it within 5 business days.
Keep that state's release gate closed and tell Distribution it is out of the launch.
Record the excluded state on the determination log and the release gate record.
checklist.done: every state excluded through an objection has a reason, a new filing path, an open determination and a closed release gate.

checklist.step: Analyse objection themes back into the package checklist
actions: Each quarter group all objection items by classification and identify the three most frequent causes.
For each recurring cause add or sharpen a line in the package checklist used in REG-016-C02 so the defect is caught before submission.
Brief the filing team on the changes and record the briefing date and attendees.
Track whether the objection rate for that cause falls in the following quarter.
checklist.done: the top recurring objection causes have new checklist lines, a briefed team and a tracked follow-up rate.

checklist.step: Archive the objection thread with the filing record
actions: File every objection letter, draft, clearance, submitted response and amended document under the product and SERFF tracking number.
Record the objection date, response date and day count on the filing record so timeliness is evidenced without re-opening SERFF.
Apply the 7-year-from-withdrawal retention label.
Index the thread by SERFF tracking number, form number and objection classification.
checklist.done: the full objection thread is archived with day counts recorded, retention-labelled and indexed by tracking number and classification.

testing.step: Build the population of objections received in the quarter
actions: Export from SERFF Filing Correspondence every objection letter issued by the Commission on the company's Compact filings in the quarter.
Capture filing tracking number, objection date, stated response date, number of items and the date any response was submitted.
Reconcile the export to the objection log and resolve every objection present in one and absent from the other.
Sign the population as complete with the export date and filter criteria.
testing.done: the SERFF correspondence export reconciles to the objection log with no unexplained items on either side.

testing.step: Reconcile objection items to logged rows and owners
actions: Count the numbered items in each sampled objection letter and compare to the number of log rows created for it.
Confirm each row has a classification, a named owner and internal draft and clearance dates set inside the response deadline.
List letters logged as a single row despite carrying multiple items as exceptions, since items get lost that way.
Quantify the proportion of objections logged on the day of receipt.
testing.done: item counts reconcile to log rows and every row carries a classification, an owner and internal dates.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample weighted to late and multi-round objections
actions: Take 100% of objections answered after the stated response date, answered inside the last 3 days, or left unanswered.
Take 100% of filings that went to a second or later objection round.
Take 15 further objections at random using a seeded, reproducible selection, including any covering Alaska.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers every late, near-deadline, unanswered and multi-round objection.

testing.step: Recompute the response day counts against the stated deadline
actions: For each population row compute days from objection date to response submission date and days from response date to the stated deadline.
Count every response submitted after the stated date as a fail and record how many days late.
Count responses submitted inside the last 3 days and compare the proportion to the 10% escalation trigger.
Confirm any extension relied on was requested in writing before the original deadline and that the Commission's revised date was met.
testing.done: day counts are recomputed for the whole population with late responses counted and every extension verified as pre-deadline.

testing.step: Re-read the responses for item-by-item completeness
actions: Open each sampled objection letter and its response letter side by side in SERFF.
Tick each numbered item off against the response and record any item answered partially, deferred or not answered at all.
Confirm every item that changed a document names the amended form number and edition date and that the amended file is attached to the schedule.
Treat a response that promises follow-up without an extension request as a fail.
testing.done: every numbered item in each sampled objection is traced to a complete answer with named amended documents.

testing.step: Verify actuarial and counsel clearances on the sample
actions: For each sampled actuarial item confirm a filing actuary answer exists naming the model version and valuation date, and a re-signed certification where a certified figure changed.
For each item conceding non-conformity or arguing an interpretation, confirm a dated Regulatory Counsel clearance pre-dates submission.
Confirm any amended rate schedule triggered a re-reconciliation instruction to Pricing before implementation.
Record missing or post-dated clearances as control failures.
testing.done: every actuarial and interpretive response item on the sample carries a pre-dated, named clearance.

testing.step: Re-perform one conformance judgement per sampled objection
actions: For each sampled objection pick the most substantive item and read the cited Uniform Standard section as it stood at the objection date.
Read the filed form text and reach an independent view on whether the filing conformed, before reading the company's response.
Compare your view to the response and record any case where the company argued conformance that the standard does not support.
Capture the standard section and form page relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled objection has an independent conformance view with the standard section and form page captured.

testing.step: Test the downstream effect of amended editions
actions: For each sampled objection that amended a form, confirm the product change record and the configuration ticket name the amended edition.
Confirm the superseded edition is not configured as available in any member state.
Where a state was excluded through an objection, confirm its release gate is closed and a state-path determination exists.
Record any live superseded edition as a reportable breach.
testing.done: amended editions flow through to the product and configuration records with no superseded edition live and excluded states gated.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the SERFF tracking number, objection item, days late and the product impact.
Assign a root cause — objection not logged per item, owner not assigned, actuarial answer late, clearance skipped, extension not requested — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any filing closed or withdrawn for non-response, record the re-filing plan and the delay to launch.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a re-filing plan where a filing lapsed.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compare late responses and lapsed filings to the zero-tolerance threshold and the near-deadline proportion to the 10% trigger.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted, cleared and submitted none of the sampled responses, sign the workpaper with the review date.
File the workpaper under REG-016-C06 and report the objection theme analysis to the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, late-response count and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Official Code Title 31)

In-scope systems.value: Compliance evidence repository as the system of record for Compact filing artefacts, indexed to the SERFF tracking number and mirrored from the document management repository

checklist.step: Open the archive record when the disposition lands
actions: On the SERFF disposition event, create the archive record keyed by SERFF tracking number under the product and writing company.
Enter the mandatory metadata: form numbers and edition dates, Compact product type, approval date, approved member states, target and actual effective dates.
Set the record status to INCOMPLETE until every required artefact is attached, and set the 10-business-day completion due date.
Link the record to the determination log row, the change ticket and the release gate record.
checklist.done: an archive record exists per disposition with full metadata, a completion due date and links to the determination, change and gate records.

checklist.step: Capture the as-filed and as-approved document sets separately
actions: Attach the package exactly as submitted — forms, Statement of Variability, certifications, actuarial memorandum, rate schedule — under an AS FILED folder.
Attach the final approved versions, including anything amended through an objection, under an AS APPROVED folder.
Where an objection changed a document, keep both versions with their dates rather than overwriting the original.
Confirm each PDF opens, is text-searchable, and shows the form number and edition date in the footer.
checklist.done: as-filed and as-approved sets exist separately, superseded versions are preserved, and every PDF opens and is searchable.

checklist.step: Attach the full correspondence thread
actions: Export from SERFF Filing Correspondence every objection letter, response letter, extension request and Commission note on the filing.
Export the filing-at-a-glance page, the submission receipt and the disposition page as dated PDFs.
Attach them to the archive record in date order with a one-line index naming each item and its date.
Record the objection round count and the response day counts on the archive record so timeliness is evidenced without re-opening SERFF.
checklist.done: the archive holds the complete dated correspondence thread with an index and the recorded response day counts.

checklist.step: Record the member-state coverage the approval delivers
actions: Write onto the archive record the exact list of member states the approval covers, taken from the approval letter, not from the submission.
Attach the dated member-roster snapshot used at determination and the snapshot current at approval.
List any state submitted but not approved with the reason and the alternative filing path taken.
Confirm Alabama, Connecticut and the District of Columbia coverage status is explicit on the record, since those jurisdictions carry the citations for this obligation.
checklist.done: the record states which member states are covered, which are not and why, with dated roster snapshots attached.

checklist.step: Apply the retention label and the destruction rule
actions: Apply the retention label of 7 years from withdrawal of the form or rate schedule, extended for the life of any in-force policy issued on the form plus the state statutory period.
Set the retention trigger to the form withdrawal event rather than a fixed date so the clock cannot start while the form is still in use.
Suppress automatic destruction while any in-force policy references the form, checked from the policy admin in-force count.
Record the retention class, trigger and computed earliest destruction date on the archive record.
checklist.done: every record carries a retention class, an event trigger, an in-force suppression and a computed earliest destruction date.

checklist.step: Index the record for regulator-style retrieval
actions: Index each record by SERFF tracking number, form number, edition date, writing company, Compact product type, approval date and each covered member state.
Confirm a search on a single member state returns every Compact-approved form available in that state.
Confirm a search on a form number returns the as-filed set, the as-approved set, the correspondence and the approval letter together.
Fix any index field that does not resolve before marking the record COMPLETE.
checklist.done: the record is retrievable by state alone and by form number alone, returning the full artefact set each time.

checklist.step: Complete and sign off the record within 10 business days
actions: Run the completeness checklist against the record: metadata, as-filed set, as-approved set, correspondence, approval letter, roster snapshots, retention label, index fields.
Chase any missing artefact from the owning team with a named due date.
Move the record status from INCOMPLETE to COMPLETE only when every line ticks, and record the signer and date.
Escalate any record still INCOMPLETE at 10 business days to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: each record is signed COMPLETE inside 10 business days or escalated with a named blocker.

checklist.step: Run the monthly incomplete-record report
actions: Report every Compact filing with a disposition but no COMPLETE archive record, with the days elapsed since disposition.
Report every archive record missing an approval letter or an as-approved form set, since those are the two artefacts an examiner asks for first.
Send the report to the Head of Compliance and the Regulatory Affairs Manager with named owners against each gap.
Track gap closure month over month and report the trend.
checklist.done: a monthly report lists every incomplete record with days elapsed and named owners, and the trend is tracked.

checklist.step: Prove retrieval with a quarterly fire drill
actions: Pick five member states at random including one of Alabama, Connecticut or the District of Columbia and request the full Compact-approved form inventory for each.
Time the retrieval from request to a complete production set and record it against the 5-business-day standard.
Check the produced set includes the approval letter, the as-approved forms and the Statement of Variability for each form.
Log any retrieval that misses the standard or returns an incomplete set as an exception.
checklist.done: a quarterly drill evidences a complete production set for five states inside 5 business days, or logs the miss.

checklist.step: Handle legal holds and examination holds
actions: On notice of litigation, a market conduct examination or a Commission enquiry touching a product, place a hold on every related filing record within 2 business days.
Suspend all destruction and disposition on held records and record the hold reason, scope and owner.
Notify the Records Manager and the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager of the hold scope in writing.
Review holds quarterly and release only with a written counsel decision.
checklist.done: every notified matter has a scoped hold applied within 2 business days, destruction suspended and a quarterly review record.

checklist.step: Control destruction with a documented review
actions: Before any destruction run, list the records whose retention trigger has matured and confirm each form is withdrawn and carries no in-force policy.
Confirm no legal or examination hold applies to any listed record.
Obtain written approval from Regulatory Counsel and the Head of Compliance on the destruction list before it executes.
Keep a permanent destruction certificate naming each record, its retention basis and the approval references.
checklist.done: no record is destroyed without a matured trigger, a no-hold confirmation, dual written approval and a destruction certificate.

checklist.step: Reconcile the archive to the SERFF filing history annually
actions: Export the company's full Compact filing history from SERFF for all writing companies since Compact registration.
Join it to the archive inventory on SERFF tracking number and list every filing with no archive record and every archive record with no SERFF filing.
Reconstruct missing records from SERFF exports and the document repository, and record the reconstruction with a Head of Compliance sign-off.
Report the reconciliation result and the reconstructed count to the Compliance Committee.
checklist.done: the archive reconciles to the full SERFF Compact history with every gap reconstructed and signed off.

checklist.step: Serve examination and Commission document requests
actions: Log every exam or Commission document request with the requesting body, the states in scope, the artefacts requested and the due date.
Task the Records Manager with the retrieval and set an internal due date at least 2 business days before the regulator's.
Have Regulatory Counsel review the production set for scope and privilege before release.
Record what was produced, to whom and when, and file the production set with the archive record.
checklist.done: each request has a logged scope, an early internal due date, a counsel-reviewed production and a filed production record.

checklist.step: Refresh the coverage record when Compact membership changes
actions: On notification of a membership change, attach the new dated roster snapshot to every archive record for a product still in force.
Annotate records whose coverage changes — a jurisdiction joining does not retroactively extend an existing approval, and a withdrawal ends coverage on its effective date.
Complete the annotation within 30 days of the membership notification.
Report the affected record count to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: every in-force product's archive record carries the current roster snapshot and a coverage annotation within 30 days of a change.

checklist.step: Run the annual archive integrity review
actions: Sample 30 archive records across products and years and open every attachment to confirm it renders and is not corrupt.
Confirm the index fields still resolve after any repository migration and that as-filed and as-approved sets remain distinguishable.
Confirm retention labels and holds survived migration with their triggers intact.
Report the integrity result and any remediation to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: an annual integrity review evidences readable attachments, resolving indexes and intact retention labels across a 30-record sample.

testing.step: Build the population of dispositions and archive records
actions: Export every Compact filing that reached a disposition in the quarter with tracking number, product, forms, approved states and disposition date.
Export the archive inventory for the same period with record status, completion date and metadata fields.
Reconcile the two on SERFF tracking number and resolve every disposition with no record and every record with no disposition.
Sign the population as complete with the export dates and queries used.
testing.done: dispositions and archive records are reconciled on tracking number with every unmatched row explained.

testing.step: Test archive completeness against the required artefact list
actions: For every population row confirm the record holds the approval letter, the as-approved form set, the as-filed set, the Statement of Variability, the certifications and the correspondence thread.
Record any record missing an approval letter or an as-approved form set as a fail under the zero-tolerance threshold.
Confirm the record was signed COMPLETE within 10 business days of disposition and record the actual day count.
Quantify completeness as a percentage of dispositions.
testing.done: every disposition has an artefact-by-artefact completeness result and a recorded completion day count.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample across ages and products
actions: Take 100% of records flagged incomplete in the monthly report during the quarter.
Take 20 records at random using a seeded, reproducible selection, spread across the current year and at least three prior years so migration effects surface.
Include at least 3 LTC or DI filings so actuarial memoranda are tested and at least 3 filings covering Alabama.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, spans multiple years and includes actuarial-bearing and Alabama-covering filings.

testing.step: Re-perform a blind retrieval against the 5-business-day standard
actions: Issue five retrieval requests phrased as an examiner would — by member state and by form number, without giving the SERFF tracking number.
Time each retrieval from request to a complete production set and compare to the 5-business-day standard.
Inspect each production set for the approval letter, the as-approved forms and the Statement of Variability.
Record any retrieval over the standard or returning an incomplete set as a fail.
testing.done: five blind retrievals are timed and inspected, with every miss of the standard recorded as a fail.

testing.step: Verify the as-approved documents against SERFF
actions: For each sampled record open the filing in SERFF Filing Access and download the approved form set from the Form Schedule.
Compare form numbers, edition dates and page counts to the archived as-approved set, and diff the text where a difference is suspected.
Confirm any document amended through an objection is archived in both its as-filed and as-approved versions.
Record any archived document that is not the approved version as a fail.
testing.done: archived as-approved documents match the SERFF approved set for every sampled record, with superseded versions preserved.

testing.step: Test the recorded member-state coverage against the approval letters
actions: For each sampled record compare the covered state list on the record to the approval letter, state by state.
Confirm any state submitted but not approved is recorded with a reason and an alternative filing path.
Confirm the roster snapshots attached carry dates around the determination and the approval, not a current download.
Record any coverage list taken from the submission rather than the approval as an exception.
testing.done: recorded coverage matches the approval letters exactly with dated roster snapshots and explained exclusions.

testing.step: Test retention labels, triggers and legal holds
actions: For each sampled record read the retention class, the trigger event and the computed earliest destruction date, and recompute it from the form withdrawal date and the in-force position.
Confirm no record with in-force policies or an open hold shows a matured destruction date.
Take the destruction log for the quarter and confirm each destroyed record had a matured trigger, no hold, and dual written approval with a destruction certificate.
Record any premature or unapproved destruction as a fail and quantify what was lost.
testing.done: retention maths recomputes, no held or in-force record is destructible, and every destruction has dual approval and a certificate.

testing.step: Reconcile the archive to the full SERFF Compact history
actions: Take the annual SERFF Compact filing history export and join it to the archive inventory on tracking number for all years within retention.
List every historical Compact approval with no archive record and quantify how many carry in-force policies.
Confirm each previously identified gap was reconstructed and signed off by the Head of Compliance.
Report the residual gap count and its in-force exposure.
testing.done: the full-history reconciliation is complete with residual gaps quantified by in-force exposure and reconstructions verified.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the SERFF tracking number, the missing artefact or failed retrieval and the regulatory exposure.
Assign a root cause — record not opened at disposition, artefact never supplied, index field wrong, retention trigger set to a fixed date, hold not applied — and an owner.
Set a remediation date and require reconstruction from SERFF where an artefact is unrecoverable internally.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a reconstruction plan where artefacts are missing.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compare missing approval letters, failed retrievals and premature destructions to the zero-tolerance thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who created and curated none of the sampled records, sign the workpaper with the review date.
File the workpaper under REG-016-C07 and report archive completeness and retrieval performance to the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, completeness rate, retrieval performance and committee reporting date exists in the repository.
